decisions.reason: Building on the established offer and having had its own webpage signals prior investment and public commitment, so management keeps it to avoid writing off sunk costs.
Its own page and explicit launch announcement show visible commitment and justify persistence despite limited recent visibility.
The launch announcement and dedicated page indicate public commitment, and its fit with the established offer makes disappointing results more attributable to temporary causes.
Two explicit launch communications and a dedicated page reveal strong public commitment and investment, so the firm is unlikely to drop it.
It is distant from the established offer, had only a mention with a quality problem, and the Valsartan issue can no longer be explained as temporary, so management is more willing to drop it.

As a distant product with only a single own page and no evidence of ongoing commitment or traction, little has been invested and the firm has not strongly committed publicly, making dropping more likely.
